info.title: Keychain
info.description: The Password Tool. On a Mac's own private wiki, the farm saves what is on its clipboard into the macOS login Keychain, lists the Keychain's generic passwords by name, and copies a value to the clipboard or hands it to the page to show briefly. Save, copy, reveal and delete are writes: only the site's signed-in owner may call them, never on a public site, and they are never offered to agents. List gives names only.

get.summary: Keychain entries by name — never values
get.description: Every generic password in the login keychain: service, account, label and modified date, read with `security dump-keychain` without -d, so no secret is read. Entries documented on token.localhost or in the Terminal plugin's vault carry a known block naming the page or vault entry.

200.description: ok, keychain, count, items[{service, account, label, modified, known}].

501.description: This farm is not on a Mac.

post.summary: Save the farm machine's clipboard into the Keychain
post.description: The value is read on the server with pbpaste — it is never in the request. It must be one line, at least eight characters and not a link. An existing entry is replaced only with overwrite. Answers with the length saved. If no token.localhost page names the service yet, a registry card is written there (names only) and listed on Token Inventory under New Entries.

service.description: The Keychain service name, e.g. example-api-token.

account.description: The Keychain account name, e.g. example. Empty matches any account.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing entry of the same service and account.

200.description: ok, message, length, replaced, cleared, and card {slug, url, title, existed} when a registry card was written or found.

400.description: A bad name, or the clipboard does not hold a key.

409.description: The entry exists; send overwrite to replace it.

post.summary: Copy a Keychain value to the farm machine's clipboard
post.description: security find-generic-password -w into pbcopy, on the server. The value never comes back — only its length. macOS may ask to allow access for entries other apps made.

service.description: The Keychain service name, e.g. example-api-token.

account.description: The Keychain account name, e.g. example. Empty matches any account.

404.description: No such entry, or access was not allowed.

post.summary: Hand a Keychain value to the owner's page, to show briefly
post.description: The one operation that returns a value. The page shows it for fifteen seconds and removes it. Owner only, private sites only, never offered to agents.

service.description: The Keychain service name, e.g. example-api-token.

account.description: The Keychain account name, e.g. example. Empty matches any account.

404.description: No such entry, or access was not allowed.

post.summary: Delete one Keychain entry — cannot be undone
post.description: security delete-generic-password for exactly one entry. confirm must repeat the service name. With no account it refuses when the service has more than one entry. The token.localhost card, if any, is kept and gets a dated Deleted line. Owner only, private sites only, never offered to agents.

account.description: The Keychain account name; needed when the service has several entries.

200.description: ok, message, and card {slug, url, title} when its registry card was marked.

409.description: Several entries share the service; give the account.
